text: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) (ការគ្រប់គ្រងសត្វល្អិតចម្រុះ) means regularly checking crops, correctly identifying the cause of damage, preventing problems where possible, and using pesticides only when justified. This matters most in the warm, humid wet season (រដូវវស្សា), which favors some insect pests and diseases, while the dry season (រដូវប្រាំង) favors other pests and adds water stress where irrigation is limited. Farmers should scout (ចុះពិនិត្យស្រែ/ចម្ការ) regularly -- checking both damaged and healthy-looking plants, including leaf undersides, stems, growing points, flowers, and fruit -- and distinguish insect damage from fungal/bacterial disease, nutrient deficiency, water stress, herbicide injury, and physical damage before deciding on control. Preventive measures: healthy planting material, locally appropriate varieties, field sanitation, weed control, avoiding excess nitrogen, appropriate spacing, crop rotation where practical, and protecting beneficial insects (សត្វល្អិតមានប្រយោជន៍) like predators and parasitoids. Do not assume pest resistance/susceptibility from a variety name alone. For vegetables and small plots, frequent hand inspection is often more practical than sophisticated monitoring equipment -- present traps, biological controls, and precision monitoring as options, not assumed defaults. Do not tell farmers to spray on a fixed calendar. If a pesticide is genuinely needed, the product must be appropriate for the crop and pest and the farmer must follow the current Cambodian product label and safety instructions; do not name a pesticide product, dose, or spray interval without verifying current Cambodian registration and formulation. Decision flow: farmer sees damage -> inspect -> determine actual cause (insect / disease / weed / nutrient / water stress / weather damage) -> assess severity -> try prevention/hand removal/cultural control first -> only then consider a verified pesticide option.
